key_concepts: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charges and is measured in amperes
Current is calculated as charge divided by time (I = q/t)
Voltage is the work per unit charge and is measured in volts
Voltage drives charges to move but does not flow through the circuit
Resistance is the opposition to current flow and is measured in ohms
Resistance depends on wire thickness, length, conductivity, and temperature
Thick, short, high-conductivity wires have lower resistance
Ohm's law states voltage equals current times resistance (V = IR)
At constant resistance, current is directly proportional to voltage
At constant voltage, current is inversely proportional to resistance
